text:
Maya Singh: Quick sync: we're sketching a "lightweight local controlplane" that lives in-customer to speed up route/license handoffs. Wanted early feedback on failure modes.
Rafael Ortiz: Benefits seem clear: lower RTT for churny routes, reduced central CP load, better on-prem resilience.
Priya Das: Main concern: key/attestation surface. Even if ephemeral, these agents will mint certs. How do we handle compromise?
Samir Iqbal: Short TTLs + signed epoch digests from central CP. Agents poll epoch; on increment they refuse old tickets. But poll frequency affects scale.
Maya Singh: Bootstrapping options: operator installer with one-time token, or console-generated join token. For cloud VMs we can use instance identity attestation.
Rafael Ortiz: Alternative: regional broker in transit path. Less install burden, preserves central trust, but added infra cost and peering config.
Priya Das: Also need clear rollback: global kill-switch that forces agents to use central endpoints, and an operator job to batch revert route mappings by region.
Samir Iqbal: Observability: per-tenant metrics (ticket latency, renew rate, last-epoch) and audit logs for bootstrap/revocation. Also a staging simulator to exercise cert rotation with connection pools.
infra-bot: Plan created "local-cp-prototype" assigned to infra-eng
Maya Singh: I'll draft a short RFC with API surface (/claim, /renew, /epoch) and migration/playbook. Will ping security for attestation requirements.
